hypothesis: beta*d_emo is redundant with gamma*d_state because e_emotional = L2_normalize(W_emo @ s_padded) is a fixed linear function of the same auto-state that d_state compares

config.relevance_definition: a stored turn is relevant iff it shares the held-out query turn's session_id
config.relevance_label_provenance: session_id ships with the corpus and was not authored for this experiment
config.query_state_condition: the 5-dim auto-state is inferred from the query text alone by a fresh AutoStateTracker and assigned to store.auto_state.state; no label information reaches the query, so no arm here is an oracle

arm_redistribution.default: none; shipped defaults from ncm/profile.py RetrievalWeights
arm_redistribution.no_emo_renorm: beta 0.2 removed, then alpha, gamma and delta each multiplied by 1/(1-0.2) = 1.25, giving 0.5, 0.375, 0.125; sum 1.0
arm_redistribution.no_emo_state_absorbs: beta 0.2 removed and added entirely to gamma, giving gamma 0.5 with alpha and delta untouched; sum 1.0

bootstrap.method: percentile bootstrap, paired, computed twice: once resampling queries and once resampling whole conversations
bootstrap.stream_note: the two bootstraps draw from two generators, seeded independently, so that each interval depends only on its own seed, the resample count and the data, and not on how many other intervals were computed first
bootstrap.unit_note: queries are not independent; every query from one conversation scores against the same store and the same candidate set, so the conversation-level interval is the one to read when the two disagree

config.shipped_artifact_scale: the files in experiments/results/exp22/ are produced at max_conversations=100, which is the script default, so running the script with no arguments reproduces them

emo_scale_invariance.definition: max over real inferred query states of the max abs component difference between encode_emotional(s) and encode_emotional(s/||s||); near zero means e_emotional depends only on the direction of the auto-state

known_no_ops: retrieve_top_k_fast ignores its s_current_normalized argument (ncm/retrieval.py:352 signature, :356 the argument, :378 reads store.auto_state.get_current_state()); it is passed here only for signature compatibility
the state channel reads the 5-dim _auto_state_cache built from MemoryEntry.auto_state_snapshot, so the 7-dim s_snapshot supplied at add() time does not enter d_state
AutoStateTracker emits 5 dimensions while SentenceEncoder.state_dim is 7, so dimensions 6 and 7 of the padded state are structurally always zero and the matching columns of W_emo never contribute
config.latency_not_measured: exp4 is the latency measurement; the two retrieval paths here have asymmetric cache treatment

dataset.random_guess_definition: mean over queries of (n_relevant / store_size); this is the expected precision at any k for a retriever drawing k memories uniformly at random, and is independent of k. It is NOT mean(n_relevant)/mean(store_size), which would divide a per-query mean by a per-conversation mean.

p@5.cluster_ci_definition: percentile bootstrap resampling whole conversations with replacement, mean taken over every query in the resampled conversations
p@5.sign_pattern: 5 changed queries favour the arm, 3 favour the reference, 220 are exactly 0.0
p@5.mde80_definition: minimum detectable effect: the smallest true mean paired difference this design would detect with 80 percent power at a two-sided 0.05 level, computed as (z_0.975 + z_0.80) * sd_delta / sqrt(n_queries) = 2.801585 * sd_delta / sqrt(n_queries). A normal approximation to the paired t-test, quoted as a scale only. It ignores the conversation clustering, so it is optimistic
p@5.wilcoxon_note: scipy.stats.wilcoxon, zero_method=wilcox, two-sided, method=exact. The exact null distribution assumes distinct absolute differences; the per-query metrics here are quantised so ties are present and no midrank correction is applied in exact mode. The exact p-value is the larger of the two and is reported for that reason. method=auto would have returned the normal approximation, which understates small-n p-values.

channel_redundancy.clustering_note: the 9401 pairs come from 228 queries in 65 conversations, so they are clustered and far from independent. No p-value is reported for either correlation for that reason; r and rho are descriptive only
channel_redundancy.channel_source: each channel is the distance returned by ncm.retrieval.retrieve_top_k_fast with all weight on that one channel, which equals the clipped channel distance exactly when every memory strength is 1.0 and contradiction awareness is off; both conditions are members of the weights-are-live guard's checks dict and therefore gate the run
channel_redundancy.d_sem_clip_note: d_sem is np.clip(1.0 - cosine_similarity, 0.0, 1.0) at ncm/retrieval.py:115, so a maximum of exactly 1.00000 is the clip boundary and not an observed extreme. Any range-based statistic involving d_sem is therefore truncated; 1503 of 9401 pairs sit on the boundary
channel_redundancy.dispersion_ratio_definition: two different dispersion measures, not interchangeable. weighted_sd_ratio_sem_over_emo is (alpha times the sd of d_sem) divided by (beta times the sd of d_emo). weighted_range_ratio_sem_over_emo is the same ratio with ranges in place of standard deviations, and its numerator is truncated by the d_sem clip. Both are pooled over all (query, memory) pairs. Each sentence that quotes a ratio names which one it is
channel_redundancy.emo_order_flip_budget_definition: beta times the range of d_emo. Two memories can be reordered by the emotional term only if the other three terms place their composite distances within this much of each other. The range is pooled over all (query, memory) pairs, which is wider than the range inside any one store, so this is an upper bound on the term's influence. The near-tie table reports the within-store version
channel_redundancy.dispersion_definition: sd is the standard deviation of that channel's distance over all (query, memory) pairs, pooled across stores; weighted_sd multiplies it by the shipped weight, giving the scale on which that channel can move the composite distance between two candidate memories

near_ties.definition: for each query, the emotional order-flip budget inside that one store is beta times the range of d_emo over the memories of that store, and the adjacent-rank gaps are the successive differences of the shipped composite distance over the top 12 memories as returned by ncm.retrieval.retrieve_top_k_fast under the default weights. A gap below the budget is a pair the emotional term could reorder on its own. The fraction is over all (query, adjacent pair) gaps, pooled across queries

weights_are_live_guard.guard_data_provenance: a real store built from the corpus, not synthetic
weights_are_live_guard.beta_live_identity: max over the memories of the guard store of |d_default - d_no_emo_renorm/1.25 - 0.2*d_emo|, where d_emo is the probe_emo_pure distance. Zero to floating point means beta contributes at its shipped value and not merely at the 1.0 used by the probe. The 'distances differ' checks above do not establish this, because the alpha, gamma and delta rescale changes every distance on its own

calibration.note: exp17's figures are means over its own query set. When max_conversations is below 100 the query set here is a prefix subset of exp17's, because the loader takes records in file order and the held-out choices are drawn from the same seeded RNG in the same order, so absolute values differ by sampling and only the paired columns are tight comparisons.

exp17_equivalence.verdict: MATCH: on the same query set this run's default arm equals exp17's ncm_inferred arm and this run's semantic_only arm equals exp17's semantic_only arm to four decimal places on all 5 reported metrics; largest absolute difference 0.00e+00

reading: The retrieval weights are proved live and beta is proved live at
its shipped 0.2, with a residual of
5.290e-08 on the identity
d_default - d_no_emo_renorm/1.25 - 0.2*d_emo, so the comparison
below is between genuinely different scorers and not between
copies.
Scale of the test: 228 queries drawn from 65 conversations.
Between the two redistributions and the three key metrics, the
number of queries whose metric actually changed ranges from
5 to 84 out of 228. Every paired
difference vector is therefore mostly exact zeros, and that has to
be read alongside any interval computed from it.
Removing the emotional term does not hurt retrieval quality on
this task. For both redistributions and all three key metrics,
zero lies strictly inside both the query-level and the
conversation-level 95 pct interval, so neither direction is
supported at that level. The point estimates weakly favour
removal: 6 of the 6 point estimates are
positive in the direction of removal, which is the direction a
redundant term would move if it were adding noise. That is a
sign pattern, not a detected effect.
What this does not license. It does not show that the emotional
channel earns none of its 0.2 weight, and it does not show that
the two arms are equivalent. A two-sided interval that contains
zero is not an equivalence test, and on difference vectors this
sparse it is close to uninformative about effect size. The
largest minimum detectable effect over these six cells is
0.0098 at 80 pct power and two-sided 0.05, so any true
effect smaller than that would have been missed by this design.
The ranking does move, so the arms are not identical
computations. The emotional term reorders results without
changing how many relevant turns land in the top k.
The semantic_only arm, which is the most consequential number
here, is not an ablation of the emotional term but a weight-free
external reference. Against the shipped composite it scores
P@5 +0.0079 with query-level CI [-0.0009, +0.0167] and
conversation-level CI [-0.0009, +0.0167], 22/228 queries changed.
NDCG@10 -0.0011 with query-level CI [-0.0050, +0.0028] and
conversation-level CI [-0.0043, +0.0022], 108/228 queries changed.
MRR +0.0072 with query-level CI [-0.0016, +0.0168] and
conversation-level CI [-0.0012, +0.0165], 16/228 queries changed.
Reading: on this corpus and this label, dropping the three
non-semantic channels entirely does not lose retrieval quality
either, and on P@5 the point estimate favours the semantic-only
retriever. That is a finding about the whole composite, not just
about beta, and it is the number a reader should be shown first.
The two channels are correlated at Pearson r = 0.4691 and Spearman
rho = 0.4767 over 9401 real (query, memory) pairs from
65 conversations. No p-value is quoted: the pairs are
clustered by query and by store, so an independence-based p-value
would be meaningless. The correlation is consistent with the
structural argument that both channels are deterministic
functions of the same normalized auto-state, so the emotional
term supplies no input the state term lacks. It is not an
algebraic identity, because the projection to 3 dimensions
distorts angles, so d_emo is not a function of d_state alone.
Mechanism. Pooled over all (query, memory) pairs, the emotional
distance has standard deviation 0.00427 against
0.15513 for the semantic distance, and after the
shipped weights that is 0.000853 against
0.062050. The channel is small in scale,
but it is not too small to act. Inside a single store its median
order-flip budget is 0.002570 against a median
adjacent-rank gap of 0.005709 in the top 12 of the
shipped composite, and
28.0 pct of those adjacent gaps (703 of
2508) are smaller than that query's
budget. So the term does reorder candidates, and the candidates it
can reorder are the ones the other three channels have already
placed within its reach. It reorders near-ties and carries no
relevance signal, which is why the ranking moves while the metrics
do not. It is not that the channel cannot separate candidates at
all.
This run measures beta only at its shipped 0.2. It says nothing
about what a larger beta would do.
Scope. One corpus, one relevance label, one query-state condition,
one encoder, one machine, and the shipped weight vector. This does
not show that an emotional channel is useless in general, and it
does not show that this one is worthless. It shows that on this
task, at this scale, removing this projection of this state does
not measurably change retrieval quality in either direction.
